title: Compare a repair branch against a reference despite unknown tensile load
statement: For a,b,c,d>0 and k>=0, reference and repair spring branches share bottom0/topDelta. Their midpoint difference is g=Delta*(c*b-a*d)/G, G=(a+b)*(c+d)+k*(a+b+c+d)>0. For Delta>0, sign(g)=sign(c*b-a*d), so the zero occurs at d=c*b/a. Positive force control has the same sign because Delta=F/Keff>0. Finite k changes signal amplitude but not this single-probe zero. Multiple finite probes require calibration of the complete coupled system.

requires: Quasistatic equilibrium of positive Hookean springs, fixed topology/common boundaries and one stiffness unit; k>=0, tensile Delta>0 or force F>0 with Keff>0.
For two thresholds, use the full coupled equilibrium and actual jointly calibrated positive reference parameters; do not copy nominal single-probe thresholds.
provides: For a,b,c,d>0 and k>=0, reference and repair spring branches share bottom0/topDelta. Their midpoint difference is g=Delta*(c*b-a*d)/G, G=(a+b)*(c+d)+k*(a+b+c+d)>0. For Delta>0, sign(g)=sign(c*b-a*d), so the zero occurs at d=c*b/a. Positive force control has the same sign because Delta=F/Keff>0. Finite k changes signal amplitude but not this single-probe zero. Multiple finite probes require calibration of the complete coupled system.
assumptions: Load magnitude independence concerns the sign/zero in this linear model, not displacement amplitude, noise margin or arbitrary service geometry.
No signal at zero excitation; compression and nonlinear material response require a different calibrated interpretation.
costs: Supply tensile excitation, displacement resolution, probe stiffness and joint reference calibration; acquire the actual mechano-fluidic transduction.
contract.units: Spring coefficients have force/length units; Delta,U,gi have length units; G has stiffness-squared units.
contract.obstruction: Acquire a stable reference and productive coupled sensing interface before treating an elastic zero crossing as completion of biological repair.

body: The reference has top a/bottom b and test top c/bottom d. Force balance gives M*u=Delta*(a,c), M=[[a+b+k,-k],[-k,c+d+k]]. Its determinant is G; subtract the two inverse-matrix solutions to obtain the gap. Positive springs give positive equivalent boundary stiffness Keff, so positive force preserves the sign. For two reference branches with Ai=ai+bi+ki, test midpoint U=Delta*[c+sum_i(ki*ai/Ai)]/[c+d+sum_i(ki)-sum_i(ki^2/Ai)]. The measured gaps are gi=[(ai+bi)*U-ai*Delta]/Ai. These are the actual code Schur complement, not two independent copies of the single-probe formula. To encode two desired crossings dH<dS, solve jointly for positive physical references satisfying g1(dH)=0 and g2(dS)=0. Existence/positive implementability must be established for the chosen design; source solver values are reports. With a valid calibration each gi decreases with d at fixed Delta>0, so its sign implements the specified crossing. Required excitation, reference drift, noise, geometry and probe backaction remain physical costs. At Delta=0 every gap is zero, and compression reverses the sign interpretation.
